units: <cite ref="Niddah 3b:44">Nidd. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>מיא שָׁרְקֵי וכ׳</he> water (when poured out of an inclined vessel) slides, but fruits do not slide (and you must invert the vessel in order to empty it).

<cite ref="Chullin 111a:10">Ḥull. 111ᵃ</cite> <he>דמא מִשְׁרַק שָׁרֵיק</he> (Ms. R. 2, a. Ar. <he>משרג שריג</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 60) blood glides off, v. <cite ref="O01635"><he>סְרַךְ</he> II</cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 30b:1">B. Kam. 30ᵇ</cite> top <he>תבנו … דמְשָׁרְקֵי</he> the Mishnah speaks of straw and stubble (deposited in the public road), because they make the ground slippery.
<cite ref="Zevachim 62a:12">Zeb. 62ᵃ</cite> <he>דלא נִשְׁתָּרְקוּ</he> (Rashi to <cite ref="Exodus 27:5">Ex. XXVII, 5</cite> <he>יִשְׁתָּרְגוּ</he>) that the priests might not slip.

<cite ref="Chullin 52a:2">Ḥull. 52ᵃ</cite> <he>כל מידי דמִישְּׁרִיק וכ׳</he> (some ed. <he>דמִשְּׁ׳</he>, Rashi <he>דמִשְׁתְּרִיק</he>; Ms. H. <he>דמשתריג … לא סריג וכ׳</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 90) in the case of an animal falling on things which slide (e.g. a pile of peas &c.), no internal injury is to be apprehended, but if it falls on things which do not slide &c.
